content.title: England v Uruguay World Cup send off 2026 — as it happened
content.text: Key moments Full-time: England 1 Uruguay 1 Valverde equalises from the spot after a foul by White Ben White gives England the lead after being booed Foden comes off after a nasty challenge from Araújo Noni Madueke forced off with an injury in a flat first half for England Buy tickets to The Times’ World Cup preview event 10.22pm March 27 Booed for scoring: White’s moment of history Wembley Stadium was emptying and any atmosphere had deflated, leaving just a few paper aeroplanes and plaintiff parps from the England band to fill the air (Jonathan Northcroft writes). You assumed those still present were lost in that glazed ennui that international friendly matches are particularly good at bringing. But then it happened, a moment of history surely. England scored. And the scorer was booed. Ben White needs to clear the air with those team-mates on whom he walked out when he left England’s World Cup camp in 2022, Tuchel had said — but turns out that is only the half of it. It appears the Arsenal defender needs to clear the air with his entire nation too. Jeered when his name was announced, jeered when he entered as a 69th-minute substitute for Fikayo Tomori, White then achieved the unique distinction of being barracked for giving his country the lead. It will take a steely mindset — from both him and Thomas Tuchel — if his international career is to continue in a climate like this. Read Jonathan Northcroft’s match report 10.16pm March 27 Ugarte had second yellow rescinded It seems that Manuel Ugarte did in fact receive two yellow cards, but the second one was rescinded, it has been claimed. 10.08pm March 27 Valverde and Núñez silence Wembley The Real Madrid midfielder taunts the home fans with Núñez, right, after his late equaliser Shutterstock 10.05pm March 27 White put through the full range of emotions White celebrates with Bowen, left, and Maguire, right, after putting England in front…Alamy … But costs his side the win by giving away a clumsy penalty in the 94th minuteGetty 9.51pm March 27 Full-time: England 1 Uruguay 1 Maguire makes two critical interventions as Uruguay threaten to score a winner. There are quite a few more boos from the home supporters at full-time, too (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). White was certainly at the centre of the drama in that second half. Booed when coming on, put England ahead, booed again, then gave away a penalty. That penalty was converted by Velverde at the death and the game ends in a draw. Tuchel is not happy at all and head straight down the tunnel. There seems to have been some confusion over a booking given to Manuel Ugarte, who received two yellow cards, but was not sent off. 9.47pm March 27 GOAL! England 1 Uruguay 1 Penalty to Uruguay (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes)! Ben White is the culprit, for kicking Federico Vinas after he attempted a shot inside the box. The raised boot was lazy. The Uruguay fans are bouncing, and they have their goal as Valverde beats Trafford from the spot. That is the first goal England have conceded since losing to Senegal last summer. 9.41pm March 27 Set pieces pay dividends for England… again Tuchel said he wanted his team to feel like a Premier League one, and scoring (yet another) set piece feels fitting (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). The England manager admitted after his last game, against Albania, that his team do “rely” on them. It feels a slightly perverse way to use all this attacking talent, but that’s true of most Premier League teams, too… 9.36pm March 27 GOAL! BEN WHITE! England 1 Uruguay 0 White scores! Palmer takes an inswinging corner, and England get a flick on through Barnes, and White taps in at the back post (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). The boos when the announcer reads out his name are vociferous, however… 9.27pm March 27 Calvert-Lewin wastes best chance yet Calvert-Lewin spurns England’s best chance of the match so far. It comes from a lovely ball in by Palmer from the edge of the 18-yard box, and the Leeds United striker glances his header wide from four yards out. It’s a poor miss from the 29-year-old. The scores remain 0-0, and some England fans are heading for the exits. 9.25pm March 27 White booed as he comes on Ben White is set to come on and make his first appearance for England since withdrawing from Gareth Southgate’s World Cup squad in 2022 (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). There is some strong booing for the Arsenal defender as his name was read out to mark his substitution. White comes on for Rashford in the second halfAFP 9.14pm March 27 Foden off for Palmer Foden tries to shake off that challenge, but can’t continue and makes way for Palmer. The Manchester City forward heads straight down the tunnel. Let’s hope he is OK. Foden is caught high on the shin by Araújo and comes off shortly after…AFP … And heads straight down the tunnelReuters Solanke also comes off for Calvert-Lewin, who is going to get his chance to impress Tuchel and make his case to be Kane’s back-up. 9.08pm March 27 Wharton offers much more in possession Adam Wharton is a much more aggressive and risky passer than anyone else in the squad (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). This quality makes him a very unusual choice for a No6, given they tend to be a bit more circumspect. But the first half showed England struggled to accelerate the game, and Wharton is a player that can turn an innocuous phase of possession into a dangerous one in a moment. I am fascinated to see how this plays out. Wharton’s best football for Crystal Palace has come when he has taken a slightly higher (No8) position, where he’s free to take lots of risks, and hit passes into the No10 on the far side. That’s not quite the dynamic here. Wharton is far more adventurous with his passing and movementGetty He is one of the best players to watch in the Premier League in my opinion. He’s so smart and forward-thinking. When your TV set at home switches to a wide angle, try to keep an eye on him and his head movement. When England have the ball, he is regularly looking around, scanning for space and to see where his team-mates and opponents are. Because of this awareness, he is happy to drop into pockets of space and then fire passes forward, or slip them between the lines. He’s already began to raise the tempo. It’s now on his team-mates to respond to the impetus he’s providing and make runs. 9.04pm March 27 Araújo lucky to not see red Foden has been completely cleaned out by Ronald Araújo and Tuchel is not happy one bit. It’s a very reckless challenge by the Uruguayan, who catches Foden high on his follow through with some real force. Tuchel, who is certain that should be a red card, has a stern word with Bielsa, the Uruguay head coach, on the touchline. Foden is OK to continue, but he is lucky not to be hurt. 9.00pm March 27 Henderson replaced by Wharton The second half is under way and Jordan Henderson has been replaced by Adam Wharton. Harry Maguire has taken over the captaincy. 8.49pm March 27 Foden struggling to make mark Here’s Foden’s first-half touchmap (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). He’s not been found between the lines much, but when he’s been on the ball, he hasn’t had the punchiness England have needed to accelerate the game. After a good start, England lost their momentum after the injury-induced break in play. Credit to Uruguay for that smart bit of game managment, since which they’ve looked stronger. 8.43pm March 27 Half-time: England 0 Uruguay 0 That’s half-time. The cameras pan to some of the England squad who are joining the team for the Japan game. They are supposedly Tuchel’s sure things… I’m not sure they’ll be worried about their World Cup spots based on what they’re watching. 8.41pm March 27 Solanke isolated and England lack width Here’s England’s first-half pass network (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). The thickness of the lines corresponds to the number of passes played between players, while the position they take is an average of their touches of the ball. So… Solanke isolated, with Foden not managing to combine with him, and arguably too far away from goal. The full backs, who are meant to be providing width and runs both inside and out, are not high enough, but this stems from England’s inability to really pin Uruguay back. We’re approaching half-time, and there’s very few players to be super-positive about. Rashford has made good runs. Henderson has looked OK (but any centre midfielder who is playing in front of a block tends to look all right). Any others? 8.31pm March 27 Rashford showing his quality In a 90 minute match, the ball is in play for about 55 minutes (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). That means, if all 22 players have an even share of the ball while it’s in play, they get just under three minutes with the ball. Of course, the defensive players tend to get more time on the ball than the attacking ones, which makes you wonder: is a few minutes on the ball enough time for these players to show what they are really about? Rashford has been England’s main threatShutterstock Editorial Some players seem keener than other to seize their moment: Rashford has just made a fantastic run all the way up the left wing, beating his man and then crossing… but nobody reaches it. 8.29pm March 27 Madueke departs with an injury Madueke makes way for Bowen. The Arsenal winger was hurt attempting to take a shot, which was blocked from close range by a Uruguay defender. Madueke kicked the back of the Uruguay defender’s footAP 8.26pm March 27 Paper aeroplanes are out… Half an hour in at Wembley and the takeaway stat so far is two… paper aeroplanes that have landed in the Uruguay six-yard box (Glenn Ebrey writes). Many more have conked fans on the back of their heads. Wembley may need to seriously consider mobile-only tickets going forward. You just can’t trust bored football fans with a sheet of A4. 8.21pm March 27 Solanke flattering to deceive I’m sitting alongside my colleague Tom Allnutt, and England have just taken a quick free kick to Dominic Solanke (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). He does well to make the run and get to the ball, but he controls it and takes it away from goal. It’s the opposite of what Harry Kane would do — I make the point to Tom, who reports on Solanke’s club, Tottenham Hotspur, for The Times. He nods knowingly, and says “I’ve seen that transition more than anyone”. 8.17pm March 27 Chance for Uruguay Tomori makes a mess of a defensive header from a regulation long ball, allowing Agustín Canobbio to run forward and get a shot away as Maguire backs off (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). There were shades of 2014 there, when Luis Suárez ran through after Steven Gerrard messed up a similar situation. 8.12pm March 27 Uruguay showing intent England (and many top clubs) are often criticised for playing a boring, slow game (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). But I think that criticism can miss the very simple fact that games are played by two teams, and if one wants to play a defensive, slow game and not contest possession, it tends to be a drab affair. Uruguay, to their credit are trying to play here, which makes it a more open game, with opportunities for both teams to break. The way Uruguay match up man-to-man means they’re just looking to win one duel in order to break forward — which Ugarte does on the edge of his box by spinning beyond Foden and advancing. 8.05pm March 27 Break in play for Uruguay injury Joaquín Piquerez, the Uruguay defender, has gone down under a challenge and is hurt (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). He went down off the pitch and made the (smart) decision to wiggle back onto it to stop England from taking the corner while his team were down to ten men. Piquerez has been replaced early on for UruguayAFP The home fans didn’t take too kindly to this, but this is exactly what any smart footballer would do, let alone in an international match at the World Cup. The question here is whether England can keep their momentum and press ahead after this break in play. They’ve started well so far, but being able to manage these stop-start moments and accelerate the game is a very important skill. 8.00pm March 27 England using ‘meat wall’ tactics from corners Set pieces feel like the key theme of the Premier League this season, specifically corners (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). There are fewer overall goals this season, but more from set pieces and corners. Half of the goals that gave England the lead in qualifying came from set pieces, and today they seem to have taken a leaf out of the Premier League book by crowding around Fernando Muslera, the Uruguay goalkeeper. Jonathan Northcroft wrote about this phenomenon earlier this season, and used a phrase by the American football writer, Michael Caley — “the meat wall”. England have now got their own meat wall (in addition to “slab head” who seems to be their prime target). 7.51pm March 27 How will England cope with Bielsa-ball? What may be interesting tonight is seeing how the England midfielders deal with Uruguay’s pressing (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). Bielsa sits on his usual bucket on the sidelinesShutterstock Editorial As Leeds United fans know, Marcelo Bielsa likes his teams to press hard, man-to-man. For an England team that haven’t played much together, this will be a real test of how well they have learned each other’s tendencies. I’m fascinated to see how whoever Manuel Ugarte man-marks plays, too. The Manchester United midfielder is not the best on the ball, but he is a ferocious ball winner. 7.49pm March 27 We are under way at Wembley England take the kick-off and we are up and running. 7.47pm March 27 Kick-off moments away The Uruguay national anthem is apparently the longest in the world (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). I like it. There’s an extended instrumental piece to start and it’s bright and light. Verdi-like as someone in the press box says… (I’m not so sure about that). 7.41pm March 27 A look at the Uruguay danger men There are plenty of brilliant players in this Uruguay team by the way. Of course, we all know about Marcelo Bielsa, the head coach, from his time at Leeds United, and we know how his teams play. Expect some heavy-metal football. Valverde is Uruguay’s talismanGetty Federico Valverde is without doubt the superstar in this Uruguay side. The Real Madrid midfielder bagged a hat-trick against Manchester City in the Champions League earlier this month. They have some strong defenders too. Barcelona’s Ronald Araújo and Atletico Madrid’s José María Giménez are rock solid at the back. And who could forget Darwin Núñez? 7.38pm March 27 Tuchel: Show me effort and intensity The countdown to this summer’s World Cup is officially on, and Thomas Tuchel has a clear message for his players tonight. “Buy into it. Buy into the ideas. Put the effort in. Put the intensity in your effort and support each other. These are the main headlines,” he told ITV. “Through training we gave them [tonight’s debutants Garner and Trafford] the headlines you just heard and then I told them that we always want the perfect match and the perfect training, but I am long enough a coach now to know that things can become difficult when you face a strong opponent. “Some players are new, hearing my voice for the first time, training with us for the first time, hearing the ideas for the first time. So I know not everything is perfect from the start or throughout the match but like I said stick together.” 7.34pm March 27 Maguire: It’s special to be back Harry Maguire, who has returned to form at Manchester United under Michael Carrick, is making his first start for England since Thomas Tuchel took over as head coach. “It’s a great feeling to play at this beautiful stadium,” he told ITV this evening. “It is always special, whether that’s for club or country, but it is a long time since I have done it so it’s a great feeling to be back. Maguire is starting alongside Tomori in defence for EnglandGetty “Every time you step onto the pitch for your country it is a chance to impress. I do see it [tonight’s game] as another opportunity. Tonight is a good occasion to go out there and produce a performance. “The form of the team [at United] and myself has improved since we changed formation. We’ve picked up many more points. So it’s a big credit to him and a big credit to myself to make sure I’m in this squad.” 7.23pm March 27 What has happened to Alexander-Arnold? Alexander-Arnold, centre, celebrates with Kyle Walker, left, Jordan Pickford and Ivan Toney during the Euro 2024 quarter-final victory over SwitzerlandCharlotte Wilson/Offside/Offside via Getty Images Thomas Tuchel has never been afraid to make decisions that cause a stir and calling up Ben White is a humdinger. With one selection, he sparked two controversies (Jonathan Northcroft writes). The first is over White himself. Tuchel has spoken of the need to “worship every moment” in the England camp, whether you are the manager, staff or a player. He wants people around him and playing for him who are “on it” from the moment an international get-together begins. Read more White must clear air with his England team-mates, says Tuchel Tuchel: Trent is not out of World Cup picture How compatible is that with the history of a footballer who walked out on England to fly home during a World Cup finals? The second involves a familiar Three Lions riddle: Trent Alexander-Arnold. How can one of the most gifted and decorated English talents of his generation be so far down the pecking order that he now appears to be, at minimum, his country’s seventh-choice right back? How one of England’s most gifted talents became England’s seventh-choice right back 7.19pm March 27 Tonight’s debutants… Garner, the Everton midfielder, has been in superb form this seasonGetty Trafford played brilliantly for Manchester City in the Carabao Cup finalReuters 7.18pm March 27 David Baddiel in the house! Hello from Wembley (Hamzah Khalique-Loonat writes). We have a sold out crowd today for England’s penultimate home fixture before the World Cup. There’s plenty of big names here, in the press box, too. I’ve just bumped into David Baddiel getting tucked into a bowl of rice and chicken tikka, and I’ve just had the pleasure of having a quick bite to eat with our photographers, Marc Aspland and Bradley Ormesher. Brad is taking up an unconventional position today, in the press box. You’ll have to wait a little while to see those pictures, they’re for a top-secret feature, apparently… 7.14pm March 27 Beckham: Trent is like Roberto Carlos — I’d take him to World Cup David Beckham has revealed that he thinks it would be hard for England not to take Trent Alexander-Arnold to the World Cup, speaking on talkSPORT. The Real Madrid defender was not named in the squad for these friendlies, leaving his hopes of featuring in Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup squad in doubt, but Beckham believes Alexander-Arnold still has a chance of featuring. Alexander-Arnold has returned to form at RealShutterstock “That’s why I’m not England manager, because I don’t have to make those decisions!” he said of Thomas Tuchel’s decision to leave out the former Liverpool full back. “But, I’m a massive fan of Trent, I love Trent as a player. I’ve heard so many times over the years when he was at Liverpool, when he’s at Madrid, when he’s playing for England, about, ‘Well, he’s not as good at defending as he is [attacking]’. “Well, sometimes you have to accept that… Roberto Carlos was an unbelievable defender, but he was also unbelievable going forward. He’d always go forward, and then we’d have to cover him, so those kind of things you expect. Like Alexander-Arnold, Roberto Carlo was an elite attacking threat from full backGetty – Contributor “But with Trent, would I take him? I’d find it very hard not to take someone like Trent. But then Thomas, he’s come out and said, I think I read it this morning, that there are other players that are ahead of him at the moment. “But he said ‘at the moment’, so that could change. I think you said it, tonight might prove that other players are playing that might not get in the squad, so you don’t know. “This is very close to picking a final squad, but I still think that Thomas is probably still considering about Trent as well.” 7.07pm March 27 Fifa World Cup Preview Event The eyes of the world will be on the US, Mexico and Canada from June 11. The largest-ever Fifa World Cup will feature 48 teams from every corner of the globe. Who’s in with a chance of lifting the trophy on Sunday, July 19 in the New York New Jersey Stadium? Join us on Tuesday, May 26 for an unmissable preview with a team of our finest writers. Host Tom Clarke, sports editor of The Times and his guests Martin Samuel and Jonathan Northcroft will share their expert insight, including of course how England and Scotlandwill perform on the biggest stage in the game. You can hear Tom, Martin and Jonathan throughout the tournament on The Game podcast. EVENT DETAILS Date: Tuesday, May 26 Timings: Doors open at 6pm. The event commences at 7pm and concludes at approximately 8.15pm. Location: The News Building, 1 London Bridge Street, London SE1 9GF Ticket Information: Tickets are £35 per person. Please see ticket booking page for full terms and conditions. 7.00pm March 27 Lots of new faces for Tuchel Thomas Tuchel has made 11 changes for tonight’s game, with senior debuts give to Trafford in goal and Garner in midfield. Five of these players are featuring for the first time under Tuchel. 6.55pm March 27 Follow our My World Cup series McCarthy and Keane, inset, defied the odds by reaching the tournament in Japan and South Korea As we gear up for this summer’s tournament in North America, our writers have been recalling their favourite World Cup moments. In the third piece of the series, Ian Whittell remembers when Mick McCarthy’s Ireland miraculously marched to the 2002 finals in Japan and South Korea, and Roy Keane put in the best individual performance he has ever seen When Roy Keane defied Dutch with greatest solo display I have ever seen 6.47pm March 27 Uruguay team news 4-3-3: Muslera — Varela, Ronald Araujo, Olivera, Piquerez — Valverde, Ugarte, De Arrascaeta — Canobbio, Aguirre, Araújo Subs: Rochet, Mele, Gimenez, Caceres, Sanabria, De La Cruz, Martinez, Nunez, Pellistri, Vina, Rodriguez, Vinas, Torres, Rodriguez 6.39pm March 27 England team news 4-2-3-1: J Trafford — T Livramento, H Maguire, F Tomori, D Spence — J Garner, J Henderson — N Madueke, P Foden, M Rashford — D Solanke Subs: A Ramsdale, J Pickford, J Steele, L Hall, A Wharton, J Stones, C Palmer, B White, K Mainoo, D Calvert-Lewin, H Barnes, J Bowen 6.31pm March 27 England v Uruguay head-to-head record Luis Suárez broke England hearts in 2014, when Uruguay beat England 2-1 and effectively knocked them out at the group stageClive Rose/Getty Of the 11 fixtures between the sides, Uruguay have won five to England’s three, while three have ended in draws. In competitive matches, Uruguay have never lost to England. 6.25pm March 27 Could we see any World Cup bolters? Calvert-Lewin, left, and Hall are pushing for a place in Tuchel’s squadReuters These tournament preparation games are not really there for our entertainment — they are there for managers to learn. Nonetheless, Wembley is sold out tonight and only a few tickets remain for Tuesday’s meeting with Japan. And maybe there will be more frisson in the football than is usually the way in such games. Thomas Tuchel has created an audition dynamic — where hopefuls could land roles or be sent to the stalls — with his ruse of cutting players from the squad and bringing 11 more established ones in for the game against Japan next week. And history says that this is a point in the cycle where candidates can very much play themselves into a tournament squad. Hurst, Owen, Sterling … can another ‘bolter’ become a World Cup mainstay? 6.17pm March 27 England’s road to the World Cup… Uruguay — Tonight (kick-off 7.45pm) Japan — March 31 (kick-off 7.45pm) New Zealand — June 6 (kick-off TBC) Costa Rica — June 10 (kick-off TBC) England’s group L fixtures:Croatia, June 17 (9.00pm)Ghana, June 23 (9.00pm)Panama, June 26 (10.00pm) 6.05pm March 27 Who will Tuchel pick tonight? England squad in full Goalkeepers: Dean Henderson (Crystal Palace), Jordan Pickford (Everton), James Trafford (Manchester City), Aaron Ramsdale (Newcastle United), Jason Steele (Brighton & Hove Albion) Defenders: Dan Burn (Newcastle United), Marc Guéhi (Manchester City), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Ezri Konsa (Aston Villa), Tino Livramento (Newcastle United), Harry Maguire (Manchester United), Nico O’Reilly (Manchester City), Jarell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen), Djed Spence (Tottenham Hotspur), John Stones (Manchester City), Fikayo Tomori (AC Milan) Midfielders: Elliot Anderson (Nottingham Forest), Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), James Garner (Everton), Jordan Henderson (Brentford), Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United), Declan Rice (Arsenal), Morgan Rogers (Aston Villa), Adam Wharton (Crystal Palace) Forwards: Jarrod Bowen (West Ham United), Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), Phil Foden (Manchester City), Anthony Gordon (Newcastle United), Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Noni Madueke (Arsenal), Cole Palmer (Chelsea), Marcus Rashford (Barcelona, loan from Manchester United), Bukayo Saka (Arsenal), Dominic Solanke (Tottenham Hotspur) 5.56pm March 27 Hello and welcome Good evening, and welcome to The Times’ live coverage of England v Uruguay. The countdown to this summer’s World Cup is officially on, and tonight, along with Tuesday’s friendly against Japan, are the final opportunities for England’s players to impress Thomas Tuchel and secure their place in the squad for this summer’s tournament in North America. We have a host of reporters in place, ready to bring you updates and analysis from Wembley — so don’t go anywhere and enjoy the game!
